title: A quasi-compact scheme is the surjective image of an affine scheme
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Its underlying space is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] if and only if there exist a commutative ring R and a scheme morphism a : Spec R → X [def-weil-affine-spectrum] which is surjective on underlying points [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The empty scheme is allowed (take the zero ring).

source.place: Section section-quasi-compact: extract a finite affine open cover; Lemma lemma-disjoint-union-affines: its finite disjoint union is affine. Formal result: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/QuasiCompact.lean, compactSpace_iff_exists, lines 196–200.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_iff_exists, whose equivalence is precisely the statement after expanding quasi-compactness and surjectivity. Its forward proof takes a finite affine open subcover and the spectrum of sections of its affine disjoint union; its reverse proof uses the continuous surjective image of the quasi-compact spectrum. The construction includes the empty coproduct, whose section ring is the zero ring.
